deviations.edit: Full local test suite deliberately NOT run. CLAUDE.md Execution Policy states 'Never run unit tests automatically - CI runs tests after commit', and the full suite is known not to complete on this machine (128M memory_limit, and -d memory_limit does not reach the test children). Ran the two relevant filtered classes instead (14 tests, 35+9 assertions, all green) and left the full sweep to CI on push.

Added a fourth change the worker left out: the invalid-link view's <title> resolved through $expired only, so a 'used'/'ineligible' render showed the heading 'You have already set your password' under a browser tab reading 'Invalid Link'. FIRST ATTEMPT used inline @if/@elseif/@else inside the <title> element; review lane claude3 correctly scored that a HIGH defect (Blade does not compile a directive whose '@' follows a word character, so @elseif/@else stayed literal text -- leaking raw Blade into the 'used' title AND blanking DEV-2246's shipped 'Link Expired' / 'Invalid Link' titles). SHIPPED APPROACH (round 2) computes the title in an @php match() block above <head> and echoes {{ $pageTitle }}; all four states verified by render probe and pinned by test_invalid_link_page_titles_are_correct_for_every_state.

Every ledger-named resource was torn down and each removal was independently verified.

ac.item: Investigate and fix the invite link signature validation issue.
ac.evidence: INVESTIGATE: complete - the defect was root-caused and fixed by DEV-2246 (PR #296 01cffb93b, PR #297 29101af15), which is contained in tags v3.8.2/v3.9.0/v3.9.1 and present on origin/deploy, so it has been live in production since 2026-08-05 - eight days AFTER DEV-2255 was filed on 2026-07-28. FIX: nothing left to fix. NOT REGRESSED, verified live over HTTPS: agent items A5 (expired -> HTTP 403, title 'Link Expired', resend guidance present) and A6 (unsigned -> HTTP 403, title 'Invalid Link'), plus B4 (git diff touches none of ValidateScoutSignedUrl.php / ScoutOnboardingNotification.php / bootstrap/app.php / config/app.php) and B3 (ScoutOnboardingNotificationTest 3 passed, 9 assertions).

ac.item: Confirm whether this affects a subset of invite links (e.g., expired/regenerated links) or all invites for certain accounts.
ac.evidence: Answered as an investigation deliverable, not a UI check. PRE-FIX it affected ALL absolute-signed onboarding links arriving behind the TLS-terminating proxy, not a subset - which is exactly why one global scheme fix (trustProxies + ForceHttpsRequest) resolved it. There are then at least TWO distinct per-account subsets: (1) guardUser()'s three rejections - already-used link, missing org_id, missing clarity-scout permission - CLOSED by this ticket and verified live by A2/A3/A4; (2) kit-less or Pennant-CLARITY_SCOUT-inactive drivers, NOT closed, verified in code (ScoutUserProvisioner sets $shouldNotify independent of $kitId and its else branch clears kit_settings; ClarityScoutAuthController:44 returns 403 'No scanner kit assigned to your account'; resend_onboarding visible() is false once email_verified_at is set). okf/concepts/scout-user-assignment.md:37 corroborates that a Scout 403 usually means a missing kit_settings row. Subset (2) is out of the approved rendering-only scope and is recorded as a residual + surfaced to the ticket owner.

ac.item: guardUser()'s 403s render the friendly invalid-link page instead of Laravel's bare 403 (derived; approved by Dalton at the question gate).
ac.evidence: All three guard branches verified live over HTTPS against the real Herd site. A2 'used' (user 3, email_verified_at set) -> HTTP 403, title 'Password Already Set — Clarity Scout', h1 'You have already set your password', body 'sign in with the password you set... contact your admin', and grep -ci resend = 0 (proving the impossible-remedy finding is fixed, since resend_onboarding is hidden for verified users). A3 'ineligible' no-permission (user 4) and A4 'ineligible' org_id-null (user 5) -> HTTP 403, title 'Account Not Eligible — Clarity Scout', h1 'This account cannot use Clarity Scout'. A1 happy path (user 2) -> HTTP 200 'Set Your Password', so the success path is intact. B2: ScoutSetPasswordControllerTest 14 passed, 52 assertions, including the ordering pin (getPermissionsTeamId unchanged at 4242, proving the org_id guard short-circuits before setPermissionsTeamId) and POST coverage for both ineligible branches.
